newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes firmer aided by weak dollar.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes firmer aided by weak dollar.

text.p: Gold fixed at its highest in over three weeks on Friday as a two-month low value for the dollar encouraged buying of the metal.
"Further weakness in the dollar is a possibility today and that is good for gold," one metals market analyst said.
Gold was fixed at $344.80 per ounce, up from $343.75 previously and a close in London of $343.65/$344.15.

The weakening of the dollar earlier this week and only partial retrieval of Wednesday's 140-point fall in the Dow Jones Industrial Average on Thursday helped re-kindle interest in gold which had been languishing.

The dollar was valued at around 122-123 yen in Europe, slightly off its overnight lows having been sold down from 128 on comments from senior Japanese ministry of finance official Eisuke Sakakibara that the yen could strengthen to 103 against the U.S. currency.
On Friday currency markets were awaiting joint intervention by central banks to support the dollar. Even so, a weaker dollar short term was not ruled out.
"We are expecting further weakening of the dollar against the yen. It's support level is not until 121.60 yen and there must be a chance of it falling that far," one technical analyst said.

Gold prices had been in a narrow range between $339-$343 since mid April in a market cowed by the threat of selling from central banks and other institutions from their reserves of over 36,000 tonnes.

"Whether or not it has the momentum to climb much higher is questionable," one dealer said, noting that so far the rally had been confined to gold market professionals and had not attracted much of the speculator business needed for a bull run.
"It can expect some very heavy selling between $346 and $347 -- if it gets there," one bullion market analyst said.
Silver prices also picked up on the weaker dollar, rallying around 10 cents on Thursday and adding another cent or so this morning to $4.84/$4.86.
"Silver has a better chance of going higher than gold. If the (investment) funds come in, there is a real chance of going through $5.00," an analyst said.
Palladium was fixed at its highest in nearly two years at $162.50 -- a dollar above the recent high set three weeks ago.
"Supplies are so tight that it is cheaper to buy spot metal than borrow it," one dealer said.
Platinum was also firmer at $383.50/$384.50, up $7.50.
